query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The application of a thin, dense alumina (Al2O3) coating via atomic layer deposition (ALD) will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) by forming a protective oxide layer that prevents further oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., Al0.5CoCrFeNi) with a coarse-grained microstructure
generation.intervention: Deposition of a 100 nm thick Al2O3 coating using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at 200°C
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 1000°C for 100 hours
generation.mechanism: The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, preventing the formation of a thick, non-protective oxide layer on the RHEA surface [Ref: none provided]
generation.predicted_outcome: A 50% reduction in oxide layer thickness (from 10 μm to 5 μm) compared to the uncoated RHEA after exposure to air at 1000°C for 100 hours
generation.baseline: Uncoated RHEA exposed to air at 1000°C for 100 hours
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 900°C to 1100°C; Atmosphere: air; Exposure time: 50 to 150 hours
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the Al2O3 coating may vary depending on the specific RHEA composition, coating thickness, and deposition conditions. Additionally, the long-term stability of the coating at high temperatures is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxide layer thickness of coated and uncoated RHEA samples after exposure to air at 1000°C for 100 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxide layer thickness of the coated RHEA is not reduced by at least 30% compared to the uncoated RHEA, the hypothesis is falsified.
